newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ACPC unity seen raising coffee prices - official.
newsitem.headline: ACPC unity seen raising coffee prices - official.

text.p: If coffee producers maintain a minimum level of discipline in regulating supply, prices should stabilise at a more remunerative level, a top Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) official said.

ACPC Secretary general Roberio Oliveira, speaking at a coffee seminar in the Brazilian city of Vitoria, pointed to the following series of factors which contribute to a more optimistic price outlook for producing nations:
* July 1996 to June 1997, in the view of the ACPC, should see relative balance in supply and demand;
* stocks continue at a level that does not give much comfort margin to the industry;
* long-term technical indicators suggest either a steady market or higher prices;
* given the market is currently in a trading range of up to 130 cents, weekly charts suggest the possibility of a move to higher levels;
* funds currently only hold one quarter of total open interest, which suggests good buying potential;
* to have any upward price movement, the market needs new buying on the part of the trade and the industry. This should certainly be seen however in the approach to the northern hemisphere winter;
* information about industry purchases and roasting levels in the U.S. suggest coffee which is being bought is being roasted immediately;
* certified stocks have never been so low.

ACPC members have agreed to regulate their exports to no more than 53.5 million 60-kg bags in the 12 months between July 1996 and June 1997 in the second year of an export program aimed at stabilising prices at higher levels.

"If producers succeed in their objectives of regulating supply, this will not only mean remunerative and stable prices for the sector as a whole but consistency in supply in terms of volume and quality," Oliveira said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
